etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French document, from Latin documentum.

definitions.definition: An original or official paper used as the basis, proof, or support of anything else, including any writing, book, or other instrument conveying information pertinent to such proof or support.

quote.citation: 1794, William Paley, View of the Evidences of Christianity:
quote.text: Saint Luke  […]  collected them from such documents and testimonies as he  […]  judged to be authentic.

definitions.definition: Any material substance on which the information is represented by writing.

quote.citation: 2012, Julie A. Jacko, editor, Human Computer Interaction Handbook, 3rd edition, CRC Press, →ISBN, page 571:
quote.text: That exception is the HTML tag–which transcludes an image into the context of the document. The image itself is neither embedded within the document nor copied—it is transcluded.

definitions.definition: (information science) An object conveying information by whatever means, capable of being indexed alongside other similar objects.

quote.citation: 2022 July 15, Alex Urban, “Mementos from digital worlds: Video game photography as documentation”, in Journal of Documentation, →DOI, →ISSN, Abstract:
quote.text: This study examines video game photography as a documentary practice.  […]  The three themes from this study's findings – that video game photographs act as (1) vehicles for storytelling, (2) creative trophies, and (3) aesthetic tokens – reveal how personally meaningful documents emerge from this medium.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) That which is taught or authoritatively set forth; precept; instruction; dogma.

quote.citation: 1741, Isaac Watts, The Improvement of the Mind:
quote.text: And particularly they should take care that the memory of the learner be not too much crowded with a tumultuous heap or overbearing multitude of documents or ideas at one time.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) An example for instruction or warning.

quote.citation: 1614, Sir Walter Raleigh, The Historie of the World:
quote.text: They were forthwith stoned to death, as a document to others.

quote.citation: 2009 May 25, “Of Memory and Israel”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: The relationship between memory as lived and history as documented is always a complex dialogue — each informing, and disinforming, the other.

quote.citation: 2015, Louise J. Wilkinson, Women in Thirteenth-Century Lincolnshire, page 92:
quote.text: Significantly, on documenting Thomas's subsequent outlawry and Margery's waivery, the court clerk recorded that it was not known whether they had any chattels because they were strangers.

definitions.definition: To furnish with documents or papers necessary to establish facts or give information.
